why: Rule 1: deg-3 junction, two proton prongs rise away to ~200k plus a 15cm e prong; zoom shows three genuinely diverging prongs.
Near rule 8 - the only real object is a 5.8cm hot stub whose p4 profile rises away from the 4000 end; all else is sub-cm unmeasured blips.
Rule 1: cool 100k start of a 24cm proton with a textbook Bragg rise to 158k; the only rival is a bare track end sitting on the z+ wall.
Rule 1 V-apex: an 11cm proton 137k->208k starts here and the 82cm MIP track back-extrapolates onto it; 15001 is the same point 1.5cm away.
The 358cm track Bragg-spikes to 145k in its last 2cm with a decay stub, so it is a stopping muon; only an isolated 1cm 90k blip is left to pick.
Rule 1: dQ/dx rises monotonically 42k->211k along the whole 66cm cluster, so 14001 is its unique cool start end.
Rule 1: deg-3 vertex with a 270cm mu and a 24cm pi both rising away to ~123k plus a flat e prong, at the most upstream z in the event.
Rule 1: deg-3 junction with two protons and a muon rising away, and the 30cm muon of the neighbouring cluster starts 1.9cm from it.
Rule 1: a 9.4cm proton (72k->180k Bragg) and a 196cm muon both start here, 66 degrees apart; the muon's far end is its own Bragg stop.
Rule 8: 14 clusters all under 2.2cm, no readable direction and no coherent shower apex, so any click is as good as any other - abstaining.
Rule 1: 2 of 2 prongs rise away - a 347cm track exiting the top wall and a 17cm prong rising to 88k - at the most upstream point z=31.
Rule 1: 2 of 2 rise away (76cm mu to 124k, 24cm p to 188k) and it is the apex of the fragmented shower band running off in -x.
Rule 1: both prongs Bragg at their far ends (160k and 220k) so it is a genuine junction, but they leave ~170 degrees apart so I drop a tier.
Start of a 120cm MIP track that exits at z=501, with a 2.4cm 217k proton stub 1.4cm away; only the id among the near co-located ends is at risk.
Deg-2 elbow with a 4.4cm 159k proton stub and a 107cm flat MIP muon that exits the z+ wall, so the muon has to start here.
